Subject: Prometheus connector proposal: LlamaPrompt + Redwood Trace SDK integration

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the intro call last week. Prometheus Labs has been prototyping a first-party connector that wires our LlamaPrompt toolkit into Redwood's Trace SDK so customers can get unified tracing and token-level attribution across prompt orchestration.

We attached a short design doc (prometheus-llamaprompt-connector-design-v1.pdf) that covers:
- connector surface (SDK shim + optional runtime sidecar)
- trace/span naming conventions for prompt fragments
- suggested canary/rollout strategy for Redwood Dedicated customers
- early security considerations (no customer tokens stored in our telemetry)

We're looking for two things from Redwood:
1) engineering review on the trace propagation approach and any pitfalls with Redwood's serving runtime (KV cache, prefix caching, batching)
2) alignment on a pilot plan (sample dataset, acceptance criteria, and a brief mutual action plan)

Can we get 30–45 minutes with your platform/telemetry folks this week? I cc'd partners@prometheus.ai for scheduling.

Attachments: prometheus-llamaprompt-connector-design-v1.pdf

Cheers,

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Prometheus connector proposal: LlamaPrompt + Redwood Trace SDK integration

Thanks for the doc and Vanessa for organizing. A few technical comments from the runtime team (brief):

> "trace/span naming conventions for prompt fragments"
- Agree standardizing a fragment id is helpful. Recommend a stable UUID per top-level request and a fragment index for sub-prompts (e.g., requestId=UUID, frag=3).

> "shim vs sidecar"
- Shim (in-process) has lower latency but makes rollout by Dedicated customers trickier (they control the runtime). Sidecar offers clearer isolation and easier canarying. For the pilot, sidecar + header-based propagation is safest.

> "KV cache interactions"
- Important: if the connector bypasses Redwood's prefix/KV cache for partial prompts, token attribution will split across spans. Two safe approaches: 1) annotate cached prefixes with the original requestId and propagate; or 2) only surface spans for non-cached generation and rely on aggregated metrics for cached hits. Approach 1 is preferred but requires a small change to our cache metadata contract. We'll sketch that in the sync.

> "latency budget"
- Pilot target: end-to-end p95 added latency < 50ms for small prompts. That's tight but achievable if sidecar runs in the same AZ and we avoid extra round trips.

I'll bring a short slide showing where the cache metadata hook would live and one or two example span grammars.

--
Jonas Weber

Vanessa / team — great feedback, thanks. Thursday 10:00 PT works for us; calendar invite sent to the addresses on this thread.

I've uploaded an updated design with a simple sequence diagram and two rollout options (shim vs sidecar) — see attachments: prometheus-llamaprompt-connector-design-v1.pdf (updated) and MA-connector-sow-draft.docx. Highlights:
- we default to sidecar for the pilot and include a shim compatibility layer for later short-circuiting in-host when customers opt-in
- connector propagates requestId + fragmentIndex in a custom header (X-Prom-ReqId) and mirrors those into Redwood Trace span attributes
- we implemented a small prototype that annotates cached prefixes with requestId; happy to demo during the sync
